gloss: furoshiki bundle; something wrapped in a furoshiki cloth

definitions.gloss: furoshiki bundle; something wrapped in a furoshiki cloth
definitions.explanation: An item or items wrapped and carried in a furoshiki, a traditional Japanese wrapping cloth. The resulting bundle is a recognizable shape in Japanese culture.

examples.japanese: {風呂敷包|ふろしきづつ}みを{手|て}に{持|も}っていた。
examples.english: She was carrying a furoshiki bundle in her hand.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}はいつも{風呂敷包|ふろしきづつ}みでお{土産|みやげ}を{持|も}ってくる。
examples.english: My grandmother always brings souvenirs wrapped in a furoshiki.

examples.japanese: {風呂敷包|ふろしきづつ}みを{解|ほど}くと、{中|なか}から{美|うつく}しい{着物|きもの}が{出|で}てきた。
examples.english: When I unwrapped the furoshiki bundle, a beautiful kimono appeared from inside.

notes:
Refers to the bundle created by wrapping items in a {風呂敷|ふろしき} (furoshiki), a square wrapping cloth. The {風呂敷|ふろしき} itself is a versatile cloth used to wrap and carry all kinds of objects, from gifts to lunch boxes to bottles. In recent years, furoshiki wrapping has gained renewed attention as an eco-friendly alternative to disposable bags.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {風呂敷包|ふろしきづつ}みを{作|つく}る: to make a furoshiki bundle
- {風呂敷包|ふろしきづつ}みを{解|ほど}く: to unwrap a furoshiki bundle
- {風呂敷包|ふろしきづつ}みを{抱|かか}える: to hold a furoshiki bundle

CULTURAL NOTE:
The image of someone carrying a {風呂敷包|ふろしきづつ}み is iconic in Japanese culture, associated with travelers, gift-giving, and traditional daily life. The expression {風呂敷|ふろしき}を{広|ひろ}げる (to spread a furoshiki) means to talk big or exaggerate.

RELATED WORDS:
- {風呂敷|ふろしき}: the wrapping cloth itself
- {包|つつ}み: wrapping, package (general term)
